hardware.name: Histórico em barras verticais
hardware.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / style-transfer. Use the supplied Suporte TI Gráfico Hardware image as the STYLE REFERENCE. Create ONE new high-fidelity UI concept board exploring BAR VISUALIZATIONS for CPU and RAM in this modern Windows technical-support app. The user chose a sober monitoring-dashboard theme and insists on a readable adaptive layout with LESS simultaneous information on smaller screens.

Preserve the same dark ink-navy/graphite shell, refined thin slate borders, azure CPU accent, teal memory accent, consistent outline icons, professional Segoe UI-like typography, white/near-white text, restrained rounded cards, no neon glow, no glass blur, no stock SaaS clutter. Preserve the app's own identity "Suporte TI Gráfico", little blue computer/pulse icon in the title bar, and native Windows minimize/maximize/close buttons. Do not add Ookla branding; this is the HARDWARE page, not an internet test.

One landscape design board with TWO fully visible front-facing desktop application windows, wider version LEFT and narrower compact version RIGHT, labelled "Janela ampla" and "Janela compacta". Both windows should fit without overlap or cropping; small desktop window is not a phone. Main title "Desempenho". Only top context tabs "Desempenho", "Discos", "Bateria", "Mais". Left large-window sidebar shows labelled groups Visão geral, Hardware (selected), Rede, Windows, Impressão, Contas e políticas, Relatórios; Configurações at bottom. Compact navigation is a narrow icon rail with an expand/hamburger button; keep the current area identifiable. Search becomes a simple icon button. One visible pause action "Pausar monitor" (compact may use an accessible-looking pause icon button).

Consistent illustrative readings across both windows: "CPU 24%" and "Memória RAM 58%", "9,3 GiB em uso", "6,7 GiB disponíveis", "16 GiB total". Numbers and bar lengths must be mathematically consistent. All current-use percentage bars use a FIXED 0–100% scale; CPU 24% means approximately ONE QUARTER filled, RAM 58% means a little over HALF. Preserve readable labels and large values, not tiny fonts. No gauges/donuts/pie charts, no line charts, no network/disks/process metric walls, no temperatures or per-core data not measured by this app. Keep secondary details under a closed "Detalhes e processos" row. Status "Ao vivo · 1 amostra/s". Restrained useful tooltips only; no contradictory values such as CPU current 24 with an "Agora 54" tooltip. Small footer on the board "Conceito visual · dados ilustrativos". The image is a design concept, not a real measured computer result.
VARIANT 1: Main-board label "01 · Histórico em barras verticais". Replace the two CPU/RAM line graphs from the reference with refined VERTICAL TIME-SERIES COLUMN CHARTS. In the wide window, exactly two substantial chart cards side by side, CPU and RAM. Each has large current number, fixed 0–100% vertical axis with 0,25,50,75,100 ticks, and a 60-second x-axis labelled "−60 s", "−30 s", "Agora". CPU has many narrow blue columns separated by fine gaps, varied heights between 15% and 42%, last column exactly 24%; memory has teal columns varying between 53% and 61%, last 58%. Rounded tops, subtle blue/teal tonal depth, no area or line plot connecting bars. A modest label "Histórico · últimos 60 s". Add CPU secondary "Média 21% · Pico 42%" only in the wider window. Used/available memory caption below the RAM chart. In the compact window, keep BOTH current readings visible as a concise paired summary, then a selector "CPU | Memória" with CPU selected and only ONE large readable column-history chart. Closed Details row below. When space shrinks, show one history at a time rather than shrinking two charts. No tiny row of extra graphics. This is the option for seeing how utilisation changes over time.

Compact window stacks the same two essential cards and keeps both percentage bars visible with their numbers; move optional history/details into one collapsed accordion. Keep pause available. VARIANT 3: Main-board label "03 · Barras segmentadas". Create a distinctive premium technical dashboard with HORIZONTAL SEGMENTED USAGE BARS. No analogue dials, no circular meters. Two strong cards for CPU and RAM. Each bar is divided into 20 evenly spaced rounded rectangular blocks with a muted dark-slate unfilled track: CPU current 24% is FOUR full blue blocks plus 80% of the fifth block, the rest unfilled; RAM current 58% is ELEVEN full teal blocks plus 60% of the twelfth, the rest unfilled. The numeric values remain exact and clearly visible even with partial segment fills. Labels 0%,50%,100% anchor both bars. Use azure only for CPU and teal only for RAM, no arbitrary rainbow alarm/green-red thresholds or gamer/retro RGB LEDs. Put "24%" and "58%" in large aligned typography, memory used/available counts in a tidy row, and a modest "Leitura atual" label. In the wide window cards may sit side by side with beautifully balanced proportions and substantial bar width. In compact window stack the cards so BOTH segmented readings remain visible and readable; keep the segments at a practical size instead of cramming extra panels. One CLOSED "Histórico dos últimos 60 s" accordion and one CLOSED "Detalhes e processos", no expanded lower analytics wall. This should feel precise, crafted and current, visually richer than ordinary progress bars while retaining the sober monitoring-dashboard family.

velocimetro:
Use case: ui-mockup / style-transfer. Redesign the supplied "Rede" two-window UI concept into a polished internet speed-test page with a prominent SPEEDOMETER GAUGE inspired by familiar Ookla Speedtest composition, while KEEPING THE APP'S OWN IDENTITY and the user's selected monitoring-dashboard design. The supplied image is the reference for Suporte TI Gráfico's exact navy/graphite styling, sidebar icons, slate borders, blue/teal accents, typography and window chrome. Do NOT put Ookla logos, Speedtest branding, advertisements, ISP logos, fake server lists, account avatars or third-party endorsements in this app.

Create ONE high-resolution landscape design board with two fully visible front-facing WINDOWS APP WINDOWS: wide version on the left and narrower compact desktop version on the right. Keep the same coherent shell as the reference: "Suporte TI Gráfico" title, little blue monitor/pulse icon beside it, native minimize/maximize/close controls, left navigation groups with "Rede" selected; compact window uses a narrow collapsible icon rail. It is a Windows desktop app, not a phone. Preserve readable type sizes and fewer simultaneous details in compact view. No perspective or external computer hardware.

Main title "Teste de velocidade". Top tabs "Conexão", "Velocidade", "IPv4", with Velocidade selected. Dark solid main surfaces, beautifully restrained blue highlights, excellent contrast, generous deliberate spacing. No neon or excessive glass.

LEFT WIDE WINDOW shows DOWNLOAD IN PROGRESS. Modest progress stepper across top: "Latência" completed, "Download" currently active, "Upload" awaiting. At center a single large, beautiful, refined semicircular speedometer: a thin precision outer scale and bold azure progress arc, subtle tick marks, scale labels from 0 to 1000 Mbps. Important tick labels "0", "250", "500", "750", "1000" in correct monotonic positions. Thin elegant pointer anchored at the bottom-center points just LEFT of the vertical midpoint for a reading of 465.9 on the 0–1000 scale. Numeric readout VERY LARGE and legible "465,9", smaller unit "Mbps", caption "Download · média da etapa". Readout, arc and needle must be consistent. Use no red/yellow/green thresholds; this is speed, not a health score.
Above or below the gauge, only two balanced metric readouts: "Download 465,9 Mbps" and "Upload —". A small latency metric "Latência HTTPS 18 ms". Below, a thin subtle real-data trace with tiny blue area fill, not a huge second dashboard. Small neutral server text "Servidor de teste: Cloudflare". A clearly available "Cancelar" action during the test, a visible but disabled "Salvar log" button, and a CLOSED "Detalhes técnicos" row. Readable consumption note "Até 1 GiB de dados por teste". Do not show jitter, packet loss, public IP, ISP or other data that this application does not collect.

RIGHT COMPACT WINDOW shows a COMPLETED RESULT so the user can evaluate the result presentation. Label this version above its window "Compacta · resultado"; label the left version "Ampla · medindo". Keep compact content clean and centered. Both completed metrics "Download 465,9 Mbps" and "Upload 40,7 Mbps" must be EQUALLY emphasized near top, with their arrow icons, and "Latência HTTPS 18 ms" smaller. A proportionally smaller semicircular gauge remains visually prominent with the same scale and shows "465,9 Mbps" explicitly captioned "Download medido"; no contradictory speed readings. Secondary details are hidden under one CLOSED "Detalhes técnicos" accordion. A clear primary "Testar novamente" button, a visible "Salvar log" button and a small copy icon/button "Copiar" at bottom. Retain the data-consumption note. Compact view should have only the essentials and this gauge, not multiple additional line charts. No clipped titles, labels or controls.

Small footer on the board "Conceito visual · dados ilustrativos". Optional modest board title "Velocímetro para o Suporte TI". The result should feel as focused and immediately understandable as a dedicated speed-test app, while clearly belonging to the same modern Suporte TI monitoring-dashboard family. This is a visual concept, not a claim of using Ookla's measurement service.
